fields.statement: Plan review round 3 left finding f1 (contradiction on run-session-idle-stall): The widened rule stalls any live run-step session idle >20 min without done, excluding only Status.Asked, usage-paused, blocked and exited. But in an owner-attended run an interactive step (e.g. a plan run's planner interviewing the owner, see rhiza-plan and the plan workflow) sits idle at its prompt waiting on the owner's reply, not on itself; Status.Asked is only set for autonomous sessions (internal/session/status.go), so such a session would be listed as 'stalled' in the inbox and run status, and the inbox's n would send it carryOn ('You have been silent...') when it is the owner who owes the next word. The Decision idle-run-session-stalls and this leaf's statement/acceptance should say how an attended session awaiting the owner is told apart (e.g. stall idle only in autonomous runs, or only for non-interactive steps), or state explicitly that it is accepted noise. The critic confirmed it: Verified: Status.Asked is set only when rec.Autonomous (internal/api/session_run.go:794-809), so an attended session's question to the owner never sets it. The plan workflow's interview step (internal/workflow/builtin/plan.toml) is an agent step that ends only on `rhiza session done` and spends most of its life idle at its prompt waiting for the owner's reply. Under run-session-idle-stall and idle-run-session-stalls, which exclude only Asked, usage-paused, blocked and exited, that session counts as stalled after 20 idle minutes. It would show in run status and the inbox, and the owner's n would send it carryOn, when it is the owner who owes the next word. The leaf and Decision must say how a session waiting on the owner is told apart, or accept that noise in so many words. How should it be settled?
